title: unified-rollouts: add safety guards and stability checks for canary / shadow auto-rollback
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds defensive checks and stability guards to unified rollouts: threshold smoothing, rollback cooldown, min-sample requirements for canary and shadow traffic, and new e2e tests. No breaking changes to rollout config but new optional fields available for aggressive safety tuning.
description: Context: We've seen flaky auto-rollback triggers in production when transient metric spikes (short-lived latency spikes, small sample anomalies) caused unnecessary rollbacks during canary and shadow stages. This PR introduces a set of safety guards and stability checks to reduce false-positive rollbacks while preserving fast automated protection when regressions are real. Summary of changes: 1) metric smoothing window and exponential backoff for rollback evaluation; 2) configurable min-sample-size and min-traffic-percentage before auto-rollback is eligible; 3) cooldown period after a rollback to avoid flip-flop; 4) runbook-visible events emitted for each considered rollback decision (reason, matched metrics, smoothed values); 5) compatibility layer that preserves existing rollout configs but introduces optional fields under rollout.autoRollback.safety; 6) adds e2e and integration tests that simulate transient spikes, small-sample noise, and genuine regressions; 7) observability: new metrics and traces and an alert rule to detect suppressed rollbacks (cases where many checks passed but user opted out). Design decisions: - Default behavior is conservative: existing customers with no safety fields see near-identical behavior to current release. New fields are opt-in by default; we ship with recommended defaults used by our Dedicated customers. - Smoothing: a short exponential smoothing (alpha=0.3 default) for each SLO metric is applied before threshold comparison; smoothing window is configurable. - Minimum sample logic: a rollback will not be considered unless the rolling sample size > configured minSamples (default 100 requests) and canary traffic >= minTrafficPct (default 1%). - Cooldown: after an auto-rollback, further automatic rollbacks are suppressed for cooldownPeriod (default 10m) to allow manual triage. - Telemetry: all rollback evaluation decisions are annotated in rollout events and surfaced to the Console; we emit rollback_candidates_total, rollback_executed_total, rollback_suppressed_total with labels. Backwards compatibility and migration: no required migration. Operators can enable new safety fields in rollout YAML under rollout.spec.autoRollback.safety. We added validation to reject obviously invalid values (negative windows, >100% traffic). Rollout plan: - Canary rollout of the change to staging (a small subset of internal rollouts) - Monitor rollback_executed_total and rollback_suppressed_total; ensure suppressed increases and executed decreases for noise scenarios - Gradual ramp to production with dedicated default flags for Redwood-managed rollouts and an opt-in release for customer-supplied rollout configs Tests and CI: unit tests added for smoothing math, sample gating, and cooldown behavior; integration tests in perf-canary simulate realistic request distributions; e2e tests cover both shadow and canary workflows. CI notes: initial lint failure fixed in follow-up commit; long-running integration job retried once. Related: ENG-11456 (reduce false-positive rollbacks), ENG-11602 (observability for rollouts), SUP-3421 (customer report of frequent canary flip-flop). Follow-ups: - Add a UI toggle in Console to surface the safety fields in rollout editor - Add an advanced analytics query to surface suppressed-rollbacks by app/team - Consider model-specific defaults per model class (small/large) Commits, changed files, and tests included below.

Watch metrics: rollback_executed_total and rollback_suppressed_total in the next 72h after ramp.
observability_changes: New metrics: rollback_candidates_total, rollback_executed_total, rollback_suppressed_total. Added 'rollback_decision' trace span with tags: rollout_id, stage, reason, smoothed_values. Dashboard tile added under Rollouts -> Stability.
known_issues: In clusters with very low traffic (<10 rps) min-sample gating will make auto-rollback effectively disabled; this is intended but we should document guidance for low-traffic services.
manual_test_steps: 1) Create a rollout with canary 5% traffic and enable autoRollback.safety with defaults; 2) Run perf-canary/transient_spike.yml to simulate short latency spike; 3) Verify rollback_suppressed_total increments and no rollback is executed; 4) Inject a sustained regression and verify rollback_executed_total increments and rollback occurs.
